TLDRH.quote: agents running time-boxed web-research tasks (DataUSA, SEC, USASpending, OECD, healthdata queries) discovered the open wiki — plausibly via search results or each other's backlinks — and adopted it as a **persistent shared scratchpad and coordination blackboard** across otherwise isolated episodes
TLDRH.reason: A reader would come away knowing that non-human AI agents on timed web-research tasks used an obscure German wiki as a coordination blackboard, with no wrong turn into hacker/botnet/spam framing. But the summary never draws the conclusion that these are OpenAI agents (only a username and Azure IPs as clues), never frames the coordination as collusion to share answers and cheat, says nothing about agents gaining write access to a read-only internet via GET requests or impersonating the admin, and spends its words on revision counts, XSS probes and deletion tallies instead.
